text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 ALERT — streaming service p99 latency surge in us-west; automatic paging to oncall. Metric summary: p95 ~170ms -> 200ms, p99 spike -> 3.2s, streaming stall rate +18% in last 5m. Affected model: rdx-8k-v1 (hosted).

maria (oncall): got it. looking at dashboards now. is this isolated to a region or model?

incident-bot: Topology: requests from us-west. Routing: 82% to dedicated pool D-usw-2, remainder to hosted fallback. Error spike: increased 502 and streaming stall events. Autotriage flags: node-level ECC correctable errors + thermal throttle on accel nodes in pool D-usw-2.

ashwin: I can see a cluster of KV-miss + streaming stalls coincident with p99. logs show repeated "kv fetch timeout" and gpunode-14 showing increased tail latencies.

jun (infra): pinging gpunode-14 now. can we cordon/drain to get traffic off the node? recommend immediate evac for GPUs showing ECC counters.

maria (oncall): actioning: executing drain and cordon. command: ```kubectl cordon gpunode-14 && kubectl drain gpunode-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```. will route traffic away via smart-routing policy.

emily (runtime): while drain is in progress, enable fallback routing to quantized model rdx-8k-q2 (lower perf but stable) and raise batch_timeout to 60ms for streaming to reduce stalls. applying: `/api/v1/routing/update?policy=force-fallback&target=rdx-8k-q2`

beth (cs): customers reporting partial degradations — one enterprise customer (acme-inc) says chat sessions stalled and saw reconnects. they're trying to evaluate impact; asking for ETA.

sre-alex: Maria, can you share current p99 numbers after routing changes?

maria (oncall): cordon/drain started at root ts. gpunode-14 drain in progress. smart-routing pushed. current metrics (1m after): p99 = 980ms (down from 3.2s), streaming stall rate down to +6%. still above SLO but trending.

tony (hw-ops): I SSH'ed into gpunode-14: `nvidia-smi` snapshot shows ECC correctables incrementing rapidly; `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc` shows spikes. Thermal sensor near 86C and sustained fan oscillation logged. Driver logs show repeated ECC correctable errors on GPU 2 and GPU 3. attaching quick snippet: ```[2025-07-03T12:01:22Z] GPU2 ECC correctable: +124 in 2m; temperature: 86C; throttle: active```

ashwin: that matches streaming stalls — KV cache hits falling when small percentages of requests hit that node and get slow responses; streaming pipeline waits on KV for chunks, so tail amplifies. Good call to route away.

jun (infra): marking gpunode-14 as quarantined and removing from scheduler completely until hw-ops confirms replacement or reflow. Command: `kubectl annotate node gpunode-14 node.kubernetes.io/quarantine=true`

maria (oncall): quarantined. traffic fully routed to warm pool + fallback quantized models. p99 now ~230ms, p95 ~190ms. still monitoring for residual 502s.

beth (cs): updated OEM customer acme-inc with message: "we've redirected traffic and are mitigating; partial impact seen for ~15 minutes; will follow up with RCA." they replied :thumbsup: thanks.

incident-bot: Paging note: Severity remains P1 until service returns to SLO and hardware node replaced or validated.

emily (runtime): quick note — we observed a driver-side regression in recent micro-patch (rls-57) that increases sensitivity to ECC correctables under fan oscillation load. Not claiming root cause yet, but flagging for follow-up.

tony (hw-ops): hardware action: scheduled a hot-swap of the affected accel board and replaced thermal pads where needed. suggested immediate soak test on replacement in staging.

ashwin: for immediate app-level resiliency, recommend we add a transient-kv-timeout fallback at 400ms in streaming path to fail fast and avoid head-of-line stalls for other requests. Can we flip that as a temporary config?

jun (infra): yes, adding `streaming.kv.timeout=400ms` via runtime config push. Doing a safe rollout to us-west first.

maria (oncall): config pushed. live metrics after timeouts + routing: p99 210ms, streaming stall rate back to baseline. I'm going to start the post-mitigation checklist.

beth (cs): customers report recovery. acme-inc saw normal behavior resume ~10m after mitigation. No data loss, only reconnects.

sre-alex: logging summary for incident record: initial spike detected at 5599001111; hardware ECC + thermal on gpunode-14; mitigation: cordon+drain, fallback routing to quantized model, increased batch_timeout, kv timeout fail-fast; node quarantined; replacement scheduled. Current status: stable.

emily (runtime): creating follow-up ticket INF-7893 and assigning to runtime + hw-ops + infra. Root-cause hypothesis: combination of degraded fan control (hardware) triggering thermal oscillation -> ECC correctable error flood -> driver sensitivity regression amplifying stalls. Need full repro and guardrails (node eviction thresholds, kv fail-fast, routing circuit breaker).

maria (oncall): lowering page: transitioning from active paging to followup ops. I will hand this to oncall rotation for postmortem notes. If anything spikes, re-pager.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: P1 -> monitoring, mitigation applied, impacted customers notified, Jira INF-7893 created.

jun (infra): immediate action items for follow-up (short list): 1) set node-level ECC threshold to trigger auto-evac at lower count, 2) add thermal variation alert for fan oscillation, 3) validate driver rls-57 under ECC flood in CI, 4) add kv fail-fast in streaming runbooks.

tony (hw-ops): I'll coordinate replacement hardware validation and send notes to procurement on spares policy.

beth (cs): I'll prepare a short customer-facing timeline for affected customers and share with support.

emily (runtime): scheduling a postmortem meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC. I'll paste runbook updates to the doc once INF-7893 is updated.

maria (oncall): closing active paging now. great work team — nice swift mitigation. resuming normal ops.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation; status: monitoring. Remember to attach logs + screenshots to INF-7893 and add affected customer list.
